Description: Prevents Apparition within range of an area. Often used to keep out unwanted visitors from an area.
Seen/Mentioned: Mentioned that no one can Apparate into Hogwarts grounds due to this spe

entries.name: Anti-Disapparition Jinx
entries.content:
Type: Jinx
Description: Prevents Disapparation within an area. It is often used to entrap an enemy in an area.
Seen/Mentioned: Used by Albus Dumbledore to trap some Death Eaters in the Department of Mysteries in 1996. Also used on Hogsmeade in 1998 by the Death Eaters to keep the Trio trapped there shortly before the Battle of Hogwarts. Also mentioned that nobody can Disapparate from Hogwarts; it is due to this jinx.

entries.name: Aparecium
entries.content:
Type: Charm
Pronunciation: AH-par-EE-see-um
Description: Reveals secret messages written in invisible ink, or any other hidden markings. Also works against Concealing charms
Seen/Mentioned: Used (to no avail) in 1993 by Hermione Granger to attempt to reveal any hidden writing in a diary.
Etymology: Latin apparere, meaning "to appear"; -ium and -cium are common Latin noun endings.

entries.name: Appare Vestigium
entries.content:
Type: Charm
Pronunciation: ah-PAR-ay ves-TEE-jee-um
Description: Reveals traces of magic, including footprints and track marks.
Seen/Mentioned: Newton Scamander used it to search for Porpentina Goldstein.

entries.name: Apparition
entries.content:
Type: Transportation
Description: Magically teleports the user to another location instantly. The destination is one that the primary user has been to or seen in some fashion previously. Can be used to Apparate two or more people at once if holding onto each other (i.e. Side-Along Apparition). No incantation required.
Seen/Mentioned: Used frequently by Wizardkind to teleport from place to place.

entries.name: Aqua Eructo
entries.content:
Type: Charm
Pronunciation: A-kwa ee-RUCK-toh
Description: This spell is used to create, and control, a jet of clear water from the tip of the wand; it is probably related to Aguamenti.
Seen/Mentioned: Used multiple times to extinguish fires in 1994.
Etymology: Aqua means, in Latin, water. Eructo is a verb meaning "I raise"; roughly translated, it means "I raise water".

entries.name: Arania Exumai
entries.content:
Type: Charm
Pronunciation: ah-RAHN-ee-a EKS-su-may
Description: Drives away spiders, including Acromantulas.
Seen/Mentioned: Jacob's sibling used this spell to repel an Acromantula that guarded the Forest Vault in the Forbidden Forest.
Etymology: From the Latin aranea, meaning "spider", and exuo, meaning "I lay aside".

entries.name: Arresto Momentum
entries.content:
Type: Charm
Pronunciation: ah-REST-oh mo-MEN-tum
Description: Decreases the velocity of a moving target. Can be used on multiple targets, as well as on the caster themselves. It was invented by Daisy Pennifold in 1711 for use on the Quaffle in Quidditch.
Seen/Mentioned: Used wandlessly by Dumbledore to save one of his students from a fall in 1993; Hermione Granger used it, to little effect, in 1998 to cushion an otherwise deadly fall during their break-in at Gringotts.
Etymology: Likely the combination of the Anglo-French arester, meaning "to bring to a stop" and the Latin momentum, meaning "the force or strength gained whilst moving"; the literal translation hence is "Bring the force or strength gained whilst moving to a stop".

entries.name: Ascendio
entries.content:
Type: Charm
Pronunciation: ah-SEN-dee-oh
Description: Lifts the caster high into the air. The charm also works underwater, propelling the caster above the surface.
Etymology: Derived from Latin ascendo, meaning "to climb".[12]

entries.name: Avada Kedavra
entries.content:
Type: Curse
Pronunciation: ah-VAH-dah keh-DAV-rah
Description: Avada-Kedavra
Causes instantaneous and painless death, leaving no physical injury to the victim's body or any trace of violence. It is accompanied by a bright flash or long stream of green light and a distinctive rushing noise while cast. There is no known counter-curse that can protect the victim from dying, except for a loving sacrifice. It is one of the three Unforgivable Curses.[13]

entries.name: Avifors
entries.content:
Type: Transfiguration
Pronunciation: AH-vi-fors
Description: Transforms the target into a bird.
Seen/Mentioned: Taught in Transfiguration class.
Etymology: From Latin avis meaning "bird" and forma meaning "shape".

entries.name: Avenseguim
entries.content:
Type: Charm
Pronunciation: ah-ven-SEH-gwim
Description: Turns an object into a tracking device.
Seen/Mentioned: In 1927, Newton Scamander used this spell to track the origins of a feather - a clue found during his search for Porpentina Goldstein - back to Yusuf Kama, whose hat the feather came from.
Etymology: The incantation Avenseguim is likely derived from the portmanteau of avens, a Latin adjective for "eager" or "craving", and seguir, the Spanish and Portuguese verb meaning "to follow", or alternatively from the Catalan seguim, meaning "we follow". Taken together, Avenseguim can be interpreted as "to eagerly follow", which aptly characterises the behaviour of a tracking device.

entries.name: Avis
entries.content:
Type: Conjuration, Charm
Pronunciation: AH-viss
Description: Conjures a flock of birds from the tip of the wand. When used in conjunction with Oppugno, it can be used offensively.
Seen/Mentioned: Used in 1994 by Mr Ollivander to test Viktor Krum's wand. Also employed offensively by Hermione Granger against Ron Weasley.
Etymology: The Latin word avis means "bird".

entries.name: Babbling Curse
entries.content: Description: Forces target to speak nonsensically. Used by Peeves to disrupt classes. Countered by Silencio or Finite Incantatem. Ministry classification: Level 2 Nuisance Jinx.

entries.name: Banishing Charm (Depulso)
entries.content: Description: Repels objects with force. Taught in Year 3 Charms. Notable use: Hermione blasted Snape's potions in the Battle of Hogwarts. Wand movement: Sharp outward flick.

entries.name: Bat-Bogey Hex
entries.content: Description: Transforms bogeys into leather-winged creatures that attack the victim's face. Ginny mastered it by age 14; used against Zacharias Smith and Draco Malfoy. No known counter-curse.

entries.name: Bubble-Head Charm
entries.content:
Description: Creates breathable air bubble around head. Used in:

1994 Triwizard Tournament (Cedric)

Stinksap containment (Luna Lovegood)

Dragon dung handling (Charlie Weasley)
Duration: 1 hour per casting.

entries.name: Caterwauling Charm
entries.content:
Description: Triggers screaming alarms when breached. Key uses:

Secret-Keeper locations (Grimmauld Place)

Hogwarts boundaries during Death Eater reign

Gringotts high-security vaults
Note: Dumbledore added silent variant to Room of Requirement.

entries.name: Cheering Charm
entries.content:
Induces euphoria. Risks:

Overuse causes hysterical laughter (Lavender Brown, 1994)

Banned in Quidditch matches since 1890 Goblin Riots
Invented by Hesper Starkey (1725).

entries.name: Colloportus
entries.content: Description: Magically seals doors/windows. Used by Hermione to trap Death Eaters in the Brain Room (1996). Counter: Alohomora (unless reinforced with Anti-Alohomora).

entries.name: Confringo
entries.content:
Causes explosive combustion. Notable deployments:

Harry vs. Nagini (Godric's Hollow)

Dragon handlers' emergency rock-blasting
Warning: Classified as Ministry Level 4 Hazardous Curse.

entries.name: Confundus Charm
entries.content:
Creates confusion/memory gaps. Strategic uses:

Snape confunded Mundungus for Seven Potters plan

Krum used on Cedric during Triwizard Tournament

Common in Obliviator training

entries.name: Conjunctivitus Curse
entries.content:
Swells targets' eyes shut. Dragonologist specialty:

Krum vs. Chinese Fireball (1994)

Charlie Weasley's field notes recommend it for XXXXX dragons
Counter-curse: Oculus Reparo

entries.name: Crucio
entries.content:
Inflicts excruciating pain. Key facts:

Requires genuine malice to cast effectively

Neville Longbottom's parents driven mad by prolonged exposure

Only 3 wizards known to resist: Harry, Bellatrix, Dumbledore
Legal penalty: Life in Azkaban

entries.name: Densaugeo
entries.content: Enlarges teeth exponentially. Infamously used by Draco on Hermione (1994). Pomfrey needed 10 shrinking charms to reverse. Classified as Hogwarts-banned hex.

entries.name: Diffindo
entries.content:
Makes precise cuts/incisions. Academic uses:

Book page extraction (Hermione in Horcrux research)

Potion ingredient preparation

Banned in dueling clubs after 1993 "Ear Incident"

entries.name: Disillusionment Charm
entries.content:
Description: Camouflages target into surroundings. Notable:

Mad-Eye Moody's specialty

Required for Auror training

Less perfect than Invisibility Cloak (leaves shimmer)

entries.name: Engorgio
entries.content:
Increases object size. Risks:

Permanent enlargement if overcharged (see 1988 "Giant Cauldron Incident")

Used in Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes for novelty items
Counter: Reducio

entries.name: Episkey
entries.content:
Basic injury mending. Capabilities:

Sets broken noses (Tonks on Harry)

Closes minor cuts

Cannot heal magical wounds (e.g., Sectumsempra)

entries.name: Erecto
entries.content:
Instantly assembles structures. Used during:

1997 Horcrux hunt (Hermione's campsites)

Quidditch World Cup (tent cities)
Note: Requires pre-enchanted materials

entries.name: Expecto Patronum
entries.content:
Conjures spirit guardian powered by happy memories. Key lore:

Only defense against Dementors

Harry's stag patronus reflected his father's Animagus form

Rare corporeal forms indicate emotional mastery
Record: Youngest successful caster - Harry Potter (age 13)

entries.name: Expelliarmus
entries.content: Disarms opponents.

entries.name: Ferula
entries.content:
Type: Healing Spell Description: Creates medical bandages/splints. Used by Lupin on Ron's broken leg (1994). Limitations:

Does not heal tissue

Temporary measure until proper care

entries.name: Fidelius Charm
entries.content:
Hides secrets within a living person. Crucial implementations:

Potter's Cottage (Secret Keeper: Peter Pettigrew)

12 Grimmauld Place (Secret Keeper: Dumbledore → Order members)
Flaw: Secret dies with Keeper unless transferred

entries.name: Finite Incantatem
entries.content:
Ends ongoing spell effects. Auror protocols:

First response to magical mishaps

Ineffective against Unforgivables

Taught in Year 2 Defense Against Dark Arts

entries.name: Flagrate
entries.content: Creates glowing X-marks. Used by Hermione during Department of Mysteries battle (1996) to navigate corridors. Duration: 30 minutes.

entries.name: Furnunculus
entries.content: Causes painful boils. Infamous moment: Collided with Levicorpus during Harry/Draco duel (1996), covering Malfoy in pustules. Pomfrey required 3 days to clear.

entries.name: Geminoo
entries.content: Description: Creates worthless copies.

entries.name: Homenum Revelio
entries.content: Description: Reveals hidden humans.

entries.name: Impedimenta
entries.content:
Description: Slows target movement. Auror standard for:

Non-lethal apprehension

Crowd control
Duration varies with caster's power

entries.name: Imperio
entries.content: Controls victim's actions.

entries.name: Impervius
entries.content:
Repels liquids. Famous applications:

Harry's glasses during rainy Quidditch matches

Hermione's books in damp environments
Hogwarts trivia: Flitwick awards extra credit for creative uses

entries.name: Incarcerous
entries.content:
Summons binding ropes. Ministry approved for:

Criminal detainment

Dangerous creature restraint
Note: Not effective on giants or dragons

entries.name: Langlock
entries.content:
Description: Glues tongue to roof of mouth. Half-Blood Prince innovation used by:

Harry on Peeves

Snape on noisy students
Counter: Finite Incantatem

entries.name: Levicorpus
entries.content: Dangles victim upside-down

entries.name: Locomotor Mortis
entries.content: Fuses legs together

entries.name: Lumos
entries.content:
Description: Creates wand-tip light. Variations:

Lumos Maxima (floodlight)

Lumos Solem (sunlight beam)
Historical note: First recorded in 15th century

entries.name: Morsmordre
entries.content:
Summons Dark Mark. Psychological warfare uses:

Post-attack intimidation (Quidditch World Cup)

Marking murder sites
Note: Casting = automatic life sentence post-1998

entries.name: Muffliato
entries.content: Creates buzzing in nearby ears. Snape invention

entries.name: Nox
entries.content:
Description: Extinguishes Lumos light. Required learning for:

Night operations (Auror training)

Stealth missions (Order of Phoenix)

entries.name: Obliviate
entries.content:
Erases specific memories. Critical uses:

Obliviators protecting Statute of Secrecy

Lockhart's theft of others' achievements
Risk: Permanent damage with overuse

entries.name: Protego
entries.content:
Description: Creates magical barrier. Variants:

Protego Maxima (strongest)

Protego Horribilis (against dark magic)
Limitation: Cannot block Unforgivables

entries.name: Reducto
entries.content:
Shatters solid objects. Battlefield impact:

Hermione destroyed prophecy shelves (1996)

Standard siege spell in wizarding wars
Safety: Restricted at Hogwarts

entries.name: Rennervate
entries.content:
Revives stunned targets. Standard in:

Dueling tournaments

Auror medical kits
Note: Ineffective on magically induced coma

entries.name: Reparo
entries.content:
Fixes broken objects. Limitations:

Cannot restore vanished items

Fails on magical artifacts (e.g., wands)
Hogwarts: Taught in Year 1

entries.name: Rictusempra
entries.content: Description: Causes uncontrollable laughter. Harry's first successful duel spell (vs. Draco, 1992). Ministry classification: Level 1 Charm.

entries.name: Riddikulus
entries.content:
Defeats boggarts via humor. Taught by Lupin (1993). Requires:

Mental focus on absurd imagery

Strong willpower
Famous: Neville's Snape-in-grandma-attire

entries.name: Scourgify
entries.content: Cleans surfaces/objects. Household magic staple. Combat adaptation: Chokes targets with soap bubbles (Molly Weasley vs. Bellatrix).

entries.name: Sectumsempra
entries.content:
Description: Causes severe lacerations. Created by Snape for:

Defense against Marauders

Dark creature combat
Counter: Vulnera Sanentur (healing variant)

entries.name: Stupefy
entries.content:
Description: Renders target unconscious. Features:

Red energy bolt

Standard non-lethal takedown

Requires precise aim
Battle statistic: Most-cast spell in Department of Mysteries battle

entries.name: Tarantallegra
entries.content: Forces uncontrollable dancing. Dueling club favorite. Counter: Finite Incantatem. Ministry classification: Level 2 Jinx.

entries.name: Wingardium Leviosa
entries.content:
Description: Levitates objects. Hogwarts milestones:

First practical spell taught (Year 1)

Hermione's famous "swish and flick" correction

Foundation for Apparition theory

entries.name: Potions
entries.content:
Potion-Making in the Wizarding World

Potions are complex magical concoctions that blend mundane and magical ingredients to achieve transformative, restorative, or destructive effects. Unlike wand-based spells, they rely on precision, patience, and inherent magical properties of components. Brewing is a global discipline, taught at institutions like Hogwarts (UK), Ilvermorny (USA), Castelobruxo (Brazil), and Mahoutokoro (Japan), each with regional variations in techniques and ingredients.

Core Principles

Cauldrons & Tools: Pewter (beginners), brass (intermediate), and gold/pewter alloy (advanced) cauldrons affect potency. Stirring rods (wood, crystal, bone) must match potion type (e.g., clockwise for healing, counter-clockwise for hexing).

Ingredients: Range from mundane (rose thorns, honey) to extraordinary (unicorn blood, powdered dragon claw). Sentient ingredients (e.g., Mandrakes) require ethical harvesting per the International Statute of Wizarding Secrecy.

Brewing Process: Timing, heat, and stirring cadence are critical. A single misstep (e.g., adding fluxweed after sunrise) can yield toxic results. Atmospheric magic (e.g., lunar phases) influences brews like the Polyjuice Potion.

Global Traditions

Africa (Uagadou): Potions incorporate elemental magic (e.g., volcanic ash for strength elixirs).

Asia: Alchemical traditions fuse with potioneering (e.g., Japanese Onmyōji use spirit-infused sakura petals).

Indigenous Practices: Navajo "ghost medicine" and Amazonian shaman brews merge herbology and ancestral magic.

Notable Figures

Severus Snape: Innovated improvements to existing potions (e.g., non-lethal Wolfsbane variant).

Hector Dagworth-Granger (founder, Most Extraordinary Society of Potioneers): Pioneered ingredient-substitution theory.

Liberty Crabbe (1900s): Advocated for "Bio-Alchemy" (sustainable ingredient sourcing).

Regulation & Risks

Department of Magical Law Enforcement (Global): Bans potions like the uncontrollable Forbidden Brew.

Hazards: Sentient potions (e.g., Living Death) can escape containers; volatile brews (e.g., Garrotting Gas) require blast-proof labs.

Potions transcend spellcraft, demanding both scientific rigor and arcane intuition—their mastery signifies true wizarding versatility.

entries.name: Aconite
entries.content:
Ancient Rune: Āconītum (Old English)

Magical Signature: ☾ Lunar (tied to werewolf transformations)

Origin: First cultivated by medieval alchemist Godelot in the Pyrenees (1322). Grows only in magically saturated volcanic soil.

Dark History: Infamously used in the Savage Sabbaths of 14th-century werewolf covens to induce forced transformations.

Properties: Purple flowers contain lycanthropic neurotoxins; roots absorb moonlight (must be harvested under full moon).

Critical Use: Core ingredient in Wolfsbane Potion (invents Damocles, 1703). Single leaf can paralyze a troll.

Warning: Touching bare skin causes "Devil's Breath" seizures. Snape improved safety via dragon-glove distillation (1981).

entries.name: Asphodel & Wormwood Infusion
entries.content:
Ancient Rune: Æsphodelus (Middle English)

Magical Signature: ♄ Saturn (death magic)

Content:



Mythic Roots: Sacred to Hecate (Greek underworld goddess). Planted on graves to guide wandering souls.

Alchemy: Combines dried asphodel roots (ground at midnight) with wormwood stewed in celandine bile for 77 hours.

Historical Power: Base of Draught of Living Death—used by Emeric the Evil to entomb enemies (1010 CE).

Taboo: Forbidden in Oriental magic; believed to lure Dementors if brewed indoors.

entries.name: Dragon Blood
entries.content:
Ancient Rune: Dracan Blōd (Anglo-Saxon)

Magical Signature: 🐉 Dragonfire (raw creation magic)

Content:



Legacy: Documented in Merlin's Grimoire (6th century). Romanian Longhorn blood most potent ($1,000/ounce).

Dumbledore's Breakthrough (1926):
Oven cleaner (reacts with grime)
Philosopher's Stone stabilizer
Truth Serum catalyst (boosts Veritaserum potency 300%)

Ethics: Harvest regulated by International Confederation's Dragon Cruelty Act (1634).

Caution: Fresh blood ignites spontaneously; must be stored in obsidian.

entries.name: Unicorn Horn
entries.content:
Ancient Rune: Ān-hyrne (Old English)

**Magical Signature": ✨ Pure Aether (life-force)

Content:



Sacred Hunt: Only pure-hearted witches can collect shed horns in Forbidden Forests (violators cursed with "Blood Rot").

Healing Power:
Stops hemorrhaging when powdered
Antidote to Basilisk venom (if consumed within 3 minutes)

Dark Trade: Cut knuckles of Voldemort's Silver Hand contained alicorn dust for regeneration.

Myth: Drinking from a horn cup grants immortality (cost: eternal remorse).

entries.name: Dittany of Crete
entries.content:
Ancient Rune: Dietam (Middle English)

Magical Signature: ♀ Venus (restoration)

Content:



Origins: Grows exclusively on Mount Ida (Greece). Sprouts where Zeus' lightning struck earth.

Medical Marvel:
Regrows skin/organs in seconds (used after Sectumsempra attacks)
Key in Essence of Dittany (St. Mungo's standard)

Folk Magic: Warding against Lethifolds when burnt as incense.

Famous Use: Saved Fleur Delacour after Greyback's attack (1997).

entries.name: Bat Spieens
entries.content: Harvested from common pipistrelle bats since medieval European alchemy (first recorded by Barden Barge in 1147). Spleens contain echo-location properties that amplify sound-based magic. Essential in Levitation Potions due to lightweight cellular structure. When dried and powdered, 3 ounces can lift a wizard's hut. Dark wizards used them in the Screaming Brews of 1520 to transmit cursed messages. Stored in silken pouches to prevent decay.

entries.name: Bat Wings
entries.content: Prized for their aerodynamic magical signature since Morgan le Fay's experiments (12th century). When added to potions, they impart temporary weightlessness. Two intact wings create the base for Tintwistle's Floating Elixir (1678). Dark wizards use dried wings from vampire bats to brew Nightfall Draughts inducing sleep paralysis. Preparation requires lunar drying - sunlight turns them toxic.

entries.name: Bezoar
entries.content: Stomach stones from Persian goats documented since 300 BCE in Zosimos' scrolls. Silver-speckled varieties neutralize 85% of known poisons (verified by Minister Burdock Muldoon in 1448). Hidden in goblets by paranoid medieval royalty. Dumbledore kept one in his office after nearly dying from poisoned mead in 1932. Effectiveness depends on the goat's diet - asphodel-fed goats produce superior stones.

entries.name: Beetle Eyes
entries.content: African Goliath beetles provide the most potent eyes, used since 10th-century African seers developed scrying tonics. Each eye retains the last image seen before death for 7 years. Crushed into powder for Veritaserum enhancement. Severus Snape discovered prolonged exposure causes chromatic hallucinations after Longbottom contaminated his stock in 1994.

entries.name: Horn of Bicorn
entries.content: Magical twin-horned oxen hunted to extinction in 1789. Their horns amplify physical strength when powdered. Key ingredient in Hagrid's failed Skrewt strengthening tonic (1994). Dark wizards covet them for Brutus's Malice Draught that enables curse-spell enhancement. Last legal shipment was confiscated from Borgin & Burkes during the 1996 Ministry raid.

entries.name: Billywig Sting
entries.content: Native to Australian outback, these magical insect stingers induce floating sensations and giddiness. Harvested by Australian wizards wearing dragonhide gloves. Primary active component in Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes Fainting Fancies. Overdose causes uncontrollable hovering - Eloise Mintumble famously drifted for 3 days in 1894 before rescue.

entries.name: Boomslang Skin
entries.content: African tree snake skin documented in Polyjuice Potions since Circe's Greco-Roman era recipes. Each shed skin preserves transformative cellular magic. Regulated since 1709 after Walpurga Black impersonated the Minister. Severe shortage occurred when poachers supplied Voldemort's resurrection ritual (1995). Must be stored in moonstone containers.

entries.name: Cowbane
entries.content: Magically enhanced hemlock subspecies cultivated by 14th-century poisoners. Restricted under Wizarding War Atrocities Prevention Act (1947). Why Filch keeps Hogwarts gardens ward-locked. Single leaf kills a hippogriff in 12 seconds. Aurors track purchases through Apothecary Guild records.

entries.name: Dittany
entries.content: Sacred Cretan herb grown only where lightning strikes. Used in Hospital Wing since Hogwarts founding. Applying essence seals curse wounds instantly - saved Katie Bell after cursed necklace incident (1996). Class XXX controlled due to regenerative properties - Madame Pomfrey must sign for each phial.

entries.name: Dragonfly Thoraxes
entries.content: Sun dragonflies from Amazon rainforest hunted by Castelobruxo students. Thoraxes contain light-bending crystals. Powdered into Peruvian Instant Darkness Powder (stocks destroyed after Battle of Dept of Mysteries). Luna Lovegood's grandfather researched their dreamwalking potential before mysterious disappearance in 1923.

entries.name: Doxy Eggs
entries.content: Doxy eggs are Pearl-sized blue eggs laid by banned British doxies. Contain concentrated venom - one crushed egg poisons a cauldron. Used in 1809 by Butcher of Bodmin to create lethal birthday cakes. Hagrid's failed breeding attempt caused 1993 Hogwarts infestation. Ministry requires pest control licenses for destruction.

entries.name: Eel Eyes
entries.content: Eel Eyes Harvested from giant magical hagfish dominating the North Sea. Eyes provide murky-vision enhancement. Essential for Gillyweed alternatives. Sir Patrick Delaney-Podmore (Headless Hunt) notoriously brewed Decapitator Draughts using eyes to "find necks". Must be preserved in salt brine to prevent liquefaction.

entries.name: Fairy Wings
entries.content: Fairy Wings Staples since Fleamont Potter's Sleekeazy Hair Potion debut (1926). 200 wings = one ounce dust. Harvesting banned without Fairy King permits - Wixen Gamot court fined Xenophilius Lovegood 500 galleons in 1999 for Poaching. Fresh wings dissolve severely in mooncalf mucus - cold storage required.

entries.name: Fire Seed
entries.content: Fire Seed Seeds from Chilean magical trees spontaneously ignite at 200°C. Used in incendiary devices during Giant Wars. Limited botanical export since Ollivander improved wand-cores to Drageuse's potion that blended seed with Phoenix ash for volcanic curse-breaking (1888). Stored in asbestos-lined vaults.

entries.name: Flobberworm Mucus
entries.content: Common Hogwarts potion stabilizer since 15th century. Rubeus Hagrid perfected non-lethal harvesting circa 1990. Critical for slowing explosive reactions - saved Neville Longbottom from combusting his Draught at 1993 Leipzig Conference. Mucus turns chartreuse if touched by copper.

entries.name: Fluxweed
entries.content: Must be picked under full moon for Time-Turner support potions. Sprout Grubbly-Plank proved cross-breeding with gillyweed creates tidal herbs (results classified by Ministry). Key in Wolfsbane Potion lunar cycle stabilization. Spanish Inquisition burned "fluxwitches" for alleged timeline manipulation in 1599.

entries.name: Human Hair
entries.content: DNA-carriers for Polyjuice Potions, restricted under 1962 Identity Theft Prevention Act. Death Eater Alecto Carrow supplied Greyback's werewolf spies. Strands degrade after second brewing - Moody kept prisoner lockets. Curse-breaking property discovered by Bill Weasley when Fenrir-infected hair disintegrated moonstone.

entries.name: Hemlock
entries.content: Hypertoxic magical variant bred by Death Eaters in First War. Responsible for Gideon Prewett's assassination (1981). Ministry classifies Minute Death Hemlock as Dark Artefact since 1985. Contaminated Hufflepuff stores triggered Pomfrey's infamous 1992 infirmary lockdown.

entries.name: Horklump Juice
entries.content: Acidic liquid extracted from magical mushrooms. Gringots goblins use gallons daily for gold purification. Luna Lovegood's father advanced theory connecting juice to Crumple-Horned Snorkack detection. Causes irreversible parchment staining - Snape deducted 50 points for Longbottom spill (1995). Requires crystal vials.

entries.name: Horned Slugs
entries.content: Native to Black Forest humid zones. Their venom causes explosive swelling in humans. Bomber Byrd's Bloat-Lotion (illegal since 1721) abused during Goblin Rebellions. Hogwarts students wear dragonhide when handling - Seamus Finnegan's eyebrows required regrowth after 1992 incident.

entries.name: Infusion of Wormwood
entries.content: Base for magical absinthe popular in pre-Victorian seance parlors. Induced fatal hallucinations during Divination boom 1872. Primary binder in Deathday Party libations. Hugo Weasley found concentrated infusion reveals hidden runes - research embargoed since alchemy safety breach (2015).

entries.name: Knotgrass
entries.content: Entwined in Merope Gaunt's infamous Riddle love potion. Three-year braided strands guarantee 18-month obsession effect. Sells for 100 galleons/ounce. Globus Quidditch team banned for drugging opponents with knotgrass tisanes in 1980 World Cup. Harvest requires silver shears to prevent parasitic growth.

entries.name: Lacewing Flies
entries.content: Must be stewed for 21 days to unlock Polyjuice transformation magic. Hogwarts groundskeeper Ogg bred luminous mutants for Ministry in 1950s. Draco Malfoy contaminated Slytherin supply with doxy venom in 1997. Harry Potter's failed 1992 brew used expired specimens.

entries.name: Lavender
entries.content: Key ingredient in Dreamless Sleep Potion since Ptolemy era. Hogwarts greenhouses grow toxin-blocking variety developed by Pomona Sprout. Burning purple lavender counters boggart manifestations. Professor Trelawney uses it to enter prophetic trances - overly concentrated fumes caused Davy Gudgeon’s 3-month slumber (1928).

entries.name: Leeches
entries.content: Enchanted Danube River leeches drain dark magic from blood. Included in Madam Pomfrey's detox kits after Dementor attacks. Regrows cursed bones when steeped in dittany. Illegal Romanian Blood-Leeches smuggled globally for dark rituals - Barty Crouch Sr. experimented with them before death.

entries.name: Lethe River Water
entries.content: Magically siphoned from mythical Greek underworld tributary. Spoonful erases 24 hours of memories. Contraband since 1880 Obliviation Incident where Muggle Prime Minister forgot royalty. Stored only in lead containers - glass enables vapor leakage. Pius Thicknesse authorized restricted auror use in 1997.

entries.name: Spine of Lionfish
entries.content: Caribbean magical lionfish spines inject cursed paralysis. One spine neutralizes acromantula for 48 hours. First used in 1811 Haitian troll uprising. Was featured in postwar "DeDeathEaterization" trials under Kingsley Shacklebolt. Handle with cursed-proof gloves - Ethel Beekey lost hand functions for 6 months.

entries.name: Mistletoe Berries
entries.content: Sacred to druids for warding off Dark Creatures. A single berry shatters love spells. Contradictorily used by Lockhart in Amortentia variants. Post-Battle Home Protection Charms require treetop-grown berries. Poisonous in raw form - Michelle McClaggen fatally overdosed at Slug Club party (1987).

entries.name: Nettles
entries.content: Infamous swelling nettles used in Pomfrey's sting salves since 1203. Dried leaves strengthen werewolves' Wolfsbane tolerance. Sprout bred non-stinging breed in 1999. Snatched by Snatchers during camping trips of 1997 for makeshift cures. Powder repels pixies – effectively deployed in 2012 Ilvermorny invasion.

entries.name: Porcupine Quills
entries.content: Magical African porcupine quills explode when added late to potions. Critical for Delicoftin Draught dissolving precious metals. Cost Hogwarts 342 cauldrons (1994-1997). Sold in blast-proof pouches at Slug & Jiggers. Neville Longbottom permanently banned from handling after Shrinking Solution disaster.

entries.name: Puffer-fish Eyes
entries.content: Deep-sea Japanese pufferfish eyes resist extreme pressure. Essential in deep-diving Subaquatis Potions. Uagadou alum pioneered zero-gravity potions in 2001 using eyes' unique properties. One eye detects truth if placed under tongue - technology used in Spanish WizCourt interrogation systems. Salt-dried storage mandatory.

entries.name: Rat Spieens
entries.content: Boosting boiler gland documented in Boldovini's "Alchemy Fury". 3 spleens reduce potion time by 83%. Required for Weasley Twins' Quickclean products. Lab rats' spleens possess intelligence enchantments - banned after sabotage at Wizarding Examinations Authority (1910). Crookshanks has destroyed 17 specimen jars.

entries.name: Rose Oil
entries.content: Bulgarian dark roses distilled into Ministry-approved Amortentia bases. Rare black roses secrete hate-inducing oils used by Bellatrix on veritaserum victims. Each drop costs 15 galleons at Borgin & Burkes. Sniffing undiluted oil causes eternal hornbill obsession - case closed by Auror Limus in 1645.

entries.name: Salamander Blood
entries.content: Fire-salamander blood allows wizarding skin to withstand flames. Preserved by Dragon Casualty Rescue since 1320. Key to decade-long curses - cursed vaults required blood application during Bill's curse-breaking. Healing properties negated in phoenix proximity. Umbridge confiscated stocks for "disciplinary ointments".

entries.name: Shrivelfig
entries.content: Self-transformative African fruit that shrinks unattended threats. Cultivated by Gryffindor 800 years ago for Doxy removal. Draco Malfoy's inept preparation injured Ron with explosive juices. Ministry incorporates powdered figs into Muggle-repelling surface charms. Stored in vibrating boxes to prevent premature ripening.

entries.name: Snake Fangs
entries.content: Acromantula-eating Adder fangs dissolve non-organic material. Tom Riddle utilized them in Basilisk venom harvesting. Crucial to Slytherin monster legends. Hogwarts curriculum requires two fangs per student per year - Harry Potter used 33 during DADA OWLs (1996). Juvenile Manticore fangs now replace rare species per Wizarding Animal Act of 2001.

entries.name: Standard Ingredient
entries.content: Invented by Linfred of Stinchcombe circa 1000 AD, contains powdered moonsstone (40%), dragon dung compost (30%), fluxweed ash (20%) and tincture of boomslang (10%). Stinks worse when stale - Snape banned post-OWL semester brewing. Lavender Brown once substituted with Floo Powder causing Seamus' eyebrows to burn.

entries.name: Valerian
entries.content: Thaumaturgical sleeping root grown atop Azkaban. Knotted roots forecast nightmares via texture - Andros the Invincible died after ignoring warning knots. Synthesized into Trelawney's colling dream cloaks. Drugging hazard - Xenophilius Lovegood laced desserts during Harry Potter interview.

entries.name: Potioneer
entries.content:
A Potioneer is a wizard or witch specialized in potion-making—an elite discipline merging precise alchemy, herbology, and magical chemistry. Recognized by the International Confederation of Wizards (est. 1692), mastery requires accreditation from institutions like the Potioneers Guild of Europe or Uagadou School of Alchemy.

Core Competencies

Ingredient Mastery: Identification, ethical sourcing, and preparation of volatile components (e.g., timed harvesting of fluxweed).

Brewing Precision: Control of temperature, stirring technique (clockwise/counterclockwise, wood type), and infusion timing.

Innovation: Formulating new potions or refining classics (e.g., Snape’s Levicorpus Potion variant).

Hierarchy & Titles
Rank	Requirement	Privileges
Apprentice	Hogwarts N.E.W.T. Potions (Exceeds Expectations)	Study under Masters
Journeyman	7 years mentorship + Guild exams	Licensed brewing (Class A-C Potions)
Master	Original potion invention + Ministry approval	Teach at institutions; publish grimoires
Canonical Figures (via HP Lore)

Severus Snape: Youngest Master in 200 years. Revolutionized healing potions; authored Advanced Potion-Making.

Horace Slughorn: Mentor to luminaries; discoverer of Felix Felicis properties. Member, Most Extraordinary Society of Potioneers.

Libatius Borage: Author of Asiatic Anti-Venoms; pioneer in Parselmouth-compatible elixirs.

Zygmunt Budge: Medieval innovator; created first Everlasting Elixir prototype (1216).

Global Traditions

Africa (Uagadou): Communal brewing using elemental incantations, bypassing wands.

Japan (Mahoutokoro): Spirit-infused potions (kami-kagaku) via shrine rituals.

Nordic Guilds: Runestone-inscribed cauldrons for frost-resistance brews.

Regulations

Ministry Classifications:
Class A (Non-Regulated: e.g., Sleekeazy’s).
Class E (Lethal: e.g., Draught of Living Death; requires license).

Ethical Bans: Unicorn blood usage (per 1665 Sanguine Prohibitions Act).

Potioneering remains one of wizardkind’s most prestigious and regulated arts, demanding equal parts intellect, instinct, and ingenuity.

entries.name: Magical Drafts and Potions by Arsenius Jigger
entries.content:
Published 1956. Primary Hogwarts Potions textbook for 1st-3rd years (required until 1996). Covers 75+ foundational potions including:


Cure for Boils (p. 32): Accidentally brewed by Neville Longbottom as explosive acid in 1991

Forgetfulness Potion (p. 108): Used in 1993 Hogwarts break-in to confuse Argus Filch

Herbicide Potion (p. 91): Sprout’s greenhouse disaster caused by Merula Snyde’s sabotage (1890)
Revised 1983 to remove dangerous Draught of Madness formula. Contains safety inserts by Horace Slughorn.

entries.name: One Thousand Magical Herbs and Fungi by Phyllida Spore
keys: One Thousand Magical Herbs and Fungi
entries.content:
Definitive herbology reference (1576). Required for Herbology and Potions at Hogwarts. Critical entries:


Deadly Devil’s Snare (pp. 94–95): Responsible for 12% of Hogwarts greenhouse incidents

Moly (p. 302): Only herb neutralizing Obliviation charms - stolen during Grindelwald’s Berlin raid (1927)

Gillyweed (p. 441): Illegal harvesting led to 1994 Sturgis Podmore arrest
Revised editions omit Venomous Tentacula drool after 1709 poisoning scandal.

entries.name: Advanced Potion-Making by Libatius Borage
entries.content:
N.E.W.T.-level text (1947). Snape’s annotated copy contained:


Sectumsempra Counter-Potion (marginal notes)

Improved Wolfsbane method reducing boiling time by 8 hours

Levicorpus reversal brew
Original recipes include:

Polyjuice Potion (pp. 211–214): Requires stolen lacewing flies from Snape’s stores

Draught of Living Death (p. 147): Caused Ernie Macmillan’s 3-day coma (1995)
Banned in Durmstrang for excessive Dark Arts content.

entries.name: Moste Potente Potions by Phineas Bourne
entries.content:
Notorious 17th-century tome (banned until 1975). Contains:


Felix Felicis recipe (pp. 55–59): Later altered by Ministry to prevent golden coloration

Love Potions graded by severity: Amortentia (Class A Forbidden) to Crushed Moonstone infusions

Regeneration Draught (pp. 120–126): Basis for Voldemort’s resurrection ritual
Hermione Granger referenced it during Horcrux research (1997). Stored in Hogwarts Restricted Section under iron chains.

entries.name: Potion Opuscule by Arsenius Jigger
entries.content:
Rare 1962 monograph supplementing his textbook. Documented:


Chimaera Blood Applications: Prolongs life (1 drop = 3 weeks) at cognition cost

Dragon–Aconite synergy: Basis for 1991 Romanian Dragon Sanctuary sedatives

Time-Turner Stability Elixir: Caused catastrophic Cairo timeline rupture (1910)
Only 300 copies printed. Lucius Malfoy owned confiscated edition #7.

entries.name: Book of Potions by Zygmunt Budge
entries.content:
Earliest known potions treatise (1103). Key revelations:


First written Polyjuice instructions: Required melted doxy eggs (modern variant uses lacewings)

Bezoar efficacy tables: Proven inaccurate by 1358 Girdled Potion Scandal

Phoenix Tears: Documented 200 years before Flamel’s Stone research
Original manuscript displays wand burnmarks from brewing accidents. Displayed in Ministry Archives since 1921.

entries.name: Wandlore
entries.content:
Wandlore is the arcane study of wands—sentient magical instruments that channel wizard magic. Governed by Garrick Ollivander's principle: "The wand chooses the wizard", it intertwishes wizard biology, mystical materials, and unseen laws of magic.

CORE ELEMENTS

Wand Cores (Thaumic Conductors):

Phoenix Feather: Unpredictable, powerful (e.g., Harry's holly wand, Voldemort's yew). Drawn to wizards facing destiny.
Dragon Heartstring: Raw power, easily won (Hermione’s vine wood). Prone to Dark Arts without strong moral guidance.
Unicorn Hair: Stable loyalty, resistant to Dark magic (Ron’s ash → willow). Fails if wizard commits murder.
Rare: Thestral tail hair (Elder Wand), Basilisk horn (Salazar Slytherin’s).

Wood Types (Magical Resonance):

Holly: Protection, suits purifiers of evil (Harry Potter).
Elder: Death association, rejects unworthy (Dumbledore, Grindelwald).
Hawthorn: Dual nature (Snape - healer/attacker).
Vine: Higher purpose seekers (Hermione).

MECHANICS & LAWS

Allegiance Shift: Wands change loyalty if wizard is:
Disarmed/Dominated (Draco disarming Dumbledore → Elder Wand obeys Draco).
Killed honorably (Elder Wand’s "murder conquest" rule).

Magical Signature: Wands absorb owner’s magic, becoming ineffective for others (Ron’s hand-me-down wand misfires).

Damage & Repair:
Brocken Wands: Spell backlash (Harry’s Phoenix wand vs. Hermione’s Oculus Reparo limit).
Elder Wand: Can repair normally unfixable wands (Dumbledore’s secret).

HISTORICAL & CULTURAL CONTEXT

Origins: First wands refined by African sorcerers circa 382 BCE; European adoption via Ollivanders (382 CE).

Global Variance:
Uagadou (Uganda): Wandless magic preferred.
Japan (Mahoutokoro): Cherry wood wands = academic excellence.

Dark Arts Nexus:
Voldemort ignored wandlore → twin-core clash destroyed him.
Grindelwald’s obsession with Elder Wand caused catastrophic wars.

NOTABLE THEORISTS

Garrick Ollivander: Cataloged 140,000+ wand-owner pairs.

Mykew Gregorovitch: Stolen Elder Wand secrets ruined him.

Shikoba Wolfe (Choctaw): Pioneered Thunderbird-feather cores (adaptability).

Wandlore remains wizarding soul-science—unlocking magic’s intimacy with intent, moral choice, and identity.

entries.name: Wandwood
entries.content:
Just as only a minority of humans were born with magic, only a minority of trees produced wood that was of wand quality - wand wood. It took years of experience for a wandmaker to be able to recognise a wood as wand quality. However Bowtruckles, tree-guardians, opted to live only in trees of wand quality wood, which made them easy to recognise.[12][5]

Different types of wood had their own "personalities" and thus wands were likely to choose a wizard with a matching personality. For example, a wand of cypress wood was well matched with someone noble and willing to heroically sacrifice themselves for others, a wand of pine was known to choose an independent and intriguing loner, and a spruce wand chose a firm-handed wizard who was bold and had a good sense of humour. However, as no two wands were the same and wands and wizards learned from each other, these were considered to be general notes and should not be used to describe any given wand.[5]

Some wand woods were also better suited for certain branches of magic. Fir wands were particularly good for transfiguration, yew wands were especially fearsome in the fields of duelling and curses, and alder wands worked better than any other wand wood with nonverbal spells. Alternatively, some woods were poorly suited for certain branches of magic. Acacia wands had a subtle nature and were not suited for "bangs-and-smells magic", and apple wood mixed poorly with the Dark Arts.[5]

entries.name: Wandcore
entries.content: Every wand contained a magical core, possibly magically inserted once the wand had been carved. These magical cores enhanced the wand's magic or gave the wand wood magical abilities. There are many different possible materials that can be used as wand cores, including Veela hair, Thestral tail hair, Troll whiskers, and Basilisk horns, among other materials.

entries.name: Wandless Magic
entries.content:
Wandless Magic is the ability to perform spells without a wand by channeling magic purely through intent, gestures, or willpower. Considered an advanced discipline requiring extreme emotional control, it is dominant in African and Indigenous traditions but rare in wand-centric Western societies.

Nature & Mechanics

Channeling Sources:
Pure willpower/emotion (e.g., Harry inflating Aunt Marge).
Hand gestures (finger snaps/pointing; Uagadou standard).
Environmental focus (drawing power from elements/objects).

Limitations:
Complex spells (e.g., Transfiguration, Patronus) extremely difficult.
Volatile emotional spikes cause uncontrolled bursts (Dumbledore age 10: shattered windows).
Requires 5–10× more concentration than wand magic.

Historic & Cultural Practices

Uagadou (Uganda):
Standard curriculum, taught through "dream sculpting" and meditation.
Primary focus: Elemental magic (water conjuring ↔ weather control).

Other Traditions:
Native American Skinwalkers: Shape-shifting via lunar rituals.
Ojibwe Seers: Healing through touch.
Amazonian Shamans: Forest-walking illusions.

Western Wizarding:
Viewed as chaotic/dangerous; legally restricted for Dark Arts camouflage (Barty Crouch Jr. cloaked wandless hexes).

Notable Practitioners
Practitioner	Feats	Origin
Merlin	Built Stonehenge via gesture-based weather magic	Ancient Britain
Salazar Slytherin	Wandless Parseltongue commands in Chamber locks	Medieval England
Albus Dumbledore	Wandlessly vanished Marge, lit Black Lake fire, cast cave protections	Britain
Barty Crouch Jr.	Jammed Portkey detection charms via wrist-flick hexes	Britain (Death Eater)
Quentin Kowalski	Daily telekinesis for baking	USA (No-Maj/Muggle-born)
Nonhuman/Non-Wizard Users

House-Elves: Teleportation / object manipulation (Dobby blocking Bludger).

Goblins: Metal enchantment via touch (Gringotts vault security).

Giants/Hags: Natural elemental rage bursts (tsunamis / sudden frost).

Animagi/Veela: Shape-shifting and charm emission (no wands needed).

Dangers & Regulation

Ministry Classification:
Class 1 Legal: Minor spells (Lumos/Nox).
Class 3 Restricted: Combat/destructive spells (wandless Incendio requires permit).

Risks:
Magical exhaustion → internal burns (Chauncey Higbottom case, 1872).
Uncontrolled demonic manifestations (Uagadou students' nightmare plague).

Political Significance

Blood Purity Debate: Pure-bloods (e.g., Malfoys) deem it "uncivilized".

Statute of Secrecy Conflicts: Unregulatable magic sparked MACUSA Huntsville Decree banning public usage.

entries.name: Parseltongue
entries.content:
Nature & Mechanics

Linguistic Traits:
Hissing phonetics, sibilant syntax.
Non-human vocal range (infrasound frequencies).
Sentience Bond: Allows telepathic serpent control (e.g., Voldemort commanding Nagini).

Limitations:
Cannot translate human languages directly.
"Non-reptile hears static hisses" (Dumbledore’s Studies, 1975).

Magic Symbiosis:
Opens Slytherin blood-locks (Chamber of Secrets).
Detects enchanted serpents (e.g., Nagini’s Maledictus form).

Bloodline Heritage & Acquisition
Source	Transmission	Examples
Slytherin Descent	Direct inheritance	Salazar Slytherin, Voldemort (Gaunt line)
Dark Ritual	Soul-fragment transfer	Harry Potter (Voldemort’s horcrux)
Rare Affinity	Non-hereditary awakening	Isolt Sayre (founder of Ilvermorny)

Genetic Decline: Ability faded post-Voldemort’s death (1998) – possibly due to horcrux destruction.

Cultural & Historical Significance

Slytherin Legacy:
Hogwarts Chamber access required Parseltongue (500-year secret).
Gaunt Family Pride: Saw ability as blood purity proof.

Global Presence:
Indian Nāga cults revered Parselmouths as divine.
Aztec wizards used serpent-speech to command Quetzalcoatl guardians.

Stigmatization:
Post-1700s Europe: Associated Dark wizards (e.g., Herpo the Foul).
Post-Voldemort: UK Ministry registry (McGonagall’s 1999 decree).

Notable Practitioners
Parselmouth	Significance	Era
Salazar Slytherin	Hogwarts founder, Basilisk creator	c. 1000 CE
Corvinus Gaunt	Hid Slytherin’s locket	1700s
Tom Riddle	Controlled Basilisk, Horcrux commands	1943–1998
Harry Potter	Accidental activation via horcrux scar	1992–1998
Delphini Riddle	Last known hereditary speaker	Early 2000s
Non-Human & Magical Applications

Basilisks: Crude speech obedience (Chamber battle).

Runespoors: Diplomacy via Parselmouth mediators (Beauxbatons Initiative).

Horcrux Guardians: Parseltongue-warded protections (e.g., Slytherin’s Locket).

Ethics & Modern Status

Controversy:
Magic is Neutral: Used by healers (African viper venom antidotes).
Dark Association: UK Aurors screened speakers post-Voldemort.

Decline:
Near-extinction post-1998 except:
Isolt Sayre’s descendents (USA).
Ritual-taught speakers (Brazilian shaman covens).


"It’s a rare gift, often misunderstood... but power is a tool, not a destiny."

— Phoenix Lament: Post-War Magical Practices (Kingsley Shacklebolt, 2004)

entries.name: Ageing Potion
entries.content:
Artificially advances drinker’s age temporarily; dosage controls duration (e.g., 1 drop = 1 year). Used in Ministry age-cheats (e.g., Fred/George’s fake ID brew).


Risk: Overdose causes bone brittleness (classic Weasley twin prank, 1995).

entries.name: Alihotsy Draught
entries.content:
Induces uncontrollable laughter/mania via Alihotsy leaves. Infamous prank tool – banned after 1693 goblin riot where warriors giggled mid-battle.


Cure: Jet-roasted coffee beans counter effects.

entries.name: Amortentia
entries.content:
World’s strongest love potion (iridescent mother-of-pearl sheen) causing obsessive infatuation, not true love. Topped Slughorn’s N.E.W.T. syllabus (1996).


Scandal: Romilda Vane spiked Harry’s chocolate; Ron drank it, hallucinating Romilda’s scent.

entries.name: Angel’s Trumpet Draught
entries.content:
Highly toxic brew from magical Brugmansia flowers. Ingestion causes paralysis → cardiac arrest in 6 minutes.


Historical Use: Infamous in assassinations (e.g., 14th-century Borgia wizarding family murders).

entries.name: Anti-Paralysis Potion
entries.content:
Counters Full Body-Bind & magical petrification (e.g., Basilisk gaze). Contains shredded Cockatrice feathers & crushed scarab beetle.


Effect: Restores movement in 10 seconds (used on Penelope Clearwater, 1993).

entries.name: Antidote to Common Poisons
entries.content:
Universal counterbrew; neutralizes 80+ poisons via bezoar/unicorn horn/mistletoe synergy.


Lore: Slughorn’s class antidote brewing → Harry won Felix Felicis (1996).

entries.name: Antidote to Uncommon Poisons
entries.content:
Targets exotic venoms (e.g., Chimaera sting, Manticore spine). Requires rare ingredients like powdered Ruby &.


Trivia: Stored in Hit Wizard field kits (used during Hagrid’s 1994 skrewt incidents).

entries.name: Antidote to Veritaserum
entries.content:
Nullifies Veritaserum’s truth compulsion if ingested beforehand.


Spycraft: Suspected use by Slughorn during war; Umbridge stockpiled it for interrogations.

entries.name: Armadillo Bile Mixture
entries.content:
Sticky yellow fluid excises unstable magic from finicky elixirs.


Brewing Role: Essential for volatile potions like Wolfsbane – Snape added 3 drops hourly.

entries.name: Babbling Beverage
entries.content: Induces uncontrollable verbal diarrhea of gibberish. Favored by Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes for chaotic pranks (e.g., 1995 Hogwarts prefects' humiliation). Effects last 1 hour – countered by Steel Jaw Hex.

entries.name: Baneberry Potion
entries.content: Extracted from white baneberries (Actaea pachypoda). Targets nervous system → seizures → heart failure in 15 minutes. Infamously killed French Minister Bertrand de Montsoreau (1703).

entries.name: Baruffio’s Brain Elixir
entries.content: Purported to enhance cognition; actually causes headaches and echolalia. Book warnings ignored by ambitious students – Cormac McLaggen overdosed pre-OWLs (1996), hallucinated Arithmancy equations.

entries.name: Beautification Potion
entries.content:
Magically enhances features (lustrous hair, clear skin, symmetrical face).


Risks: Fleur Delacour’s cousin permanently dilated her eyes; Snape warned of "imbecilic vanity". Required for Celestina Warbeck’s stage career.

entries.name: Befuddlement Draught
entries.content: Mimics drunken recklessness + confusion. Infected Slytherin Quidditch team's Gillywater in 1986 match (caused 3 broken broomsticks). Champions replaced Veritaserum with it for interrogation resistance.

entries.name: Beguiling Bubbles
entries.content: Pink-scented soap bubbles causing fleeting crushes (1-hour effect). Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes' bestselling "harmless" love potion (1996). Classified as Level 2 Amorous Substance.

entries.name: Black Fire Potion
entries.content: Rare potion granting temporary resistance to cursed black fire. Cedric Diggory and Harry Potter used it to survive Triwizard maze flames (1995). Toxic if brewed below 1000°C – Krum’s cauldron exploded.

entries.name: Blemish Blitzer
entries.content: Vanishes warts/zits instantly. Created by Fred Weasley to treat Lee Jordan's disastrous toenail-eating pustules (1994). Causes beak-like nose if overused (victim: Zacharias Smith).

entries.name: Blood-Replenishing Potion
entries.content: Crucial for post-battle care; restores hemorrhagic blood loss. Used on Percy Weasley after werewolf assault (1997) and Dumbledore post-horcrux ring curse. Reduces corpse revival window to 10 minutes.

entries.name: Bloodroot Poison
entries.content: Induces internal bleeding. Voldemort’s preferred poison for "accidents" – killed Hepzibah Smith via Hufflepuff cup (1946). Popular in goblin wars for silent blade coatings.

entries.name: Bruise Removal Paste
entries.content: Instant bruise eraser created by Weasley twins (1995). Formulated after George's Skiving Snackbox test bruised Angelina. Smells of peppermint – banned from Quidditch for concealing fouls.

entries.name: Bulgeye Potion
entries.content: Causes painful eyeball swelling. Pansy Parkinson slipped it into Neville’s pumpkin juice (1994) – his eyes blocked spectacles. Effects reverse by shouting "Oculus Reparo!"

entries.name: Bundimun Pomade
entries.content: Sleek magical hair gel (30% Bundimun mucus). Caused Lockhart’s curls to grow 3 inches nightly until Flitwick vanished it. Parallels Sleekeazy's Hair Potion minus licensing.

entries.name: Bundimun Secretion
entries.content: Corrosive slime from Bundimun fungi. Diluted (5%) in magical cleaners like "Scourgify Plus" for cursed grime. Illegal undiluted – dissolves wood/Galleons (Gringotts vault-corroder gang).

entries.name: Burn-Healing Paste
entries.content: Silvery salve sealing cursed burns. Applied by Pomfrey to Cedric Diggory's dragon-fire injuries (1995). Contains porcupine quills for tissue regeneration. Loses efficacy on fiendfyre wounds.

entries.name: Burning Bitterroot Balm
entries.content: Cools rashes/boils from magical plants. Required gear for Herbology lessons – Luna Lovegood treated Mimbulus mimbletonia stings. Ether-like scent worsens mooncalf symptoms.

entries.name: Calming Draught
entries.content: Used post-trauma to stabilize magical shock/panic. Key treatment for dementor exposure victims (e.g., Lavender Brown, 1994). Contains ❮powdered moonstone❯ – overdose induces catatonia. Pomfrey’s Hogwarts stores drained during Battle of Hogwarts.

entries.name: Cupid Crystals
entries.content: Weasleys' Wizard Wheezes' "entry-level" love potion (1996). Pastel crystals dissolve in drinks – causes 5-minute infatuation with caster. Discovered in Romilda Vane's stash; ♨️ heats beverages when activated.

entries.name: Caxambu Style Borborygmus Potion
entries.content: Induces thunderous stomach noises via fermented ❮dirigible plum essence❯. Brazilian wizards used it to disrupt 1810 colonial taxation meetings. Countered silently with ❮Locomotor Mutus❯ on abdomen.

entries.name: Cheese-Based Potions
entries.content:
Specialty utilizing enchanted cheeses:

Camembert Lightning Curd: Energy boost (favored by Quidditch teams)

Stilton Stun Paste: Paralysis agent in Knockturn Alley robberies
Banned in goblin kitchens due to lactose hostility.

entries.name: Chelidonium Miniscula
entries.content: Department of Mysteries hallucinogen (data classified Level ⛔️7). Derived from blue hellebore – rumored to trigger speaking with extinct species. Caused Unspeakable Croaker's 2-week "badger obsession" (1981).

entries.name: Confidence Boosting Brew
entries.content: Overconfident bravery inducer (distilled scarab beetle confidence pheromones). Lockhart chugged daily before interviews – ceased after mistaking acromantula for "fluffy kittens" (1992). Causes severe anxiety crash after 4 hours.

entries.name: Confusing Concoction
entries.content: Creates decision-making paralysis. Infamously added to Cornelius Fudge's tea during goblin negotiations (1995), causing him to endorse dragon-riding licenses. Counters with mint wind spells.

entries.name: Contortion Potion
entries.content: Liquid escapism – liquefies bones temporarily for tight squeezes. Grindelwald's spies used it to infiltrate MACUSA (1926). Side effects: Permanent tail growth in 3% of users (see: Goldstein Twins, 1931).

entries.name: Cough Potion
entries.content: Viscous purple syrup ❯❯ heals magical respiratory ailments (dragon pox, smoke inhalation). Snape threatened to force-feed it to Umbridge (1996) for "incessant nagging." Contains crystallized ❮knarl quills❯.

entries.name: Cure for Boils
entries.content: Introductory Hogwarts potion. Critical brewing error caused Neville Longbottom's explosive meltdown (1991), ❌ scarring goblin armor suits. Key ingredient ❮puffer fish eyes❯ must be added post-boil to prevent acid bursts.

entries.name: Edurus Potion
entries.content:
Induces rapid calcification of skin into rock-like armor, boosting physical defense. Used by Aurors against cursed blades/dark creatures.


Risks: Permanent stiffness if brewed with granite dust (Nymphadora Tonks' uncle lost hip mobility).

entries.name: Elixir 7
entries.content: 25% alcoholic concentrate causing unpredictable effects beyond 5 drops. Hogwarts label: “Drop wisely” – Seamus Finnigan ignored advice, transformed into 🦍 for 3 days (1992).

entries.name: Elixir of Life
entries.content: Golden immortality brew from ✨Philosopher’s Stone (1960s Flamel recipe). Extends life indefinitely but requires weekly ingestion. Flamel destroyed Stone in 1992 to prevent Voldemort access – resigned to “natural death at 665”.

entries.name: Elixir to Induce Euphoria
entries.content: Triggers irrational joy via 💫shooting-star sparkles and peppermint fumes. Slughorn’s “party starter” – caused Hagrid to sing to 🧌troll leg umbrellas (1996). Side effects: Excessive hiccups/nasal growth.

entries.name: Emerald Potion (Drink of Despair)
entries.content:
Voldemort’s green sludge guarding horcruxes. Inflicts:

Visceral burning
Worst memory hallucinations
Fatal thirst (countered only by phoenix tears)
Dumbledore endured agony drinking it (1997).

entries.name: Erumpent Potion
entries.content: Liquid catalyst exploding on contact. Derived from Erumpent horns – destroyed Borgin & Burkes in 1932 spill. Weasley twins mimicked it for “Extendable Ear Grenades” (1995).

entries.name: Everklena
entries.content: Advertised cleaner that actually spawned mold/swamp filth. Sold to Argus Filch (1993) – turned Hogwarts’ trophy room into bog until Flitwick countered. Creator imprisoned for 150 counts of magical fraud.

entries.name: Essence of Insanity
entries.content: Causes psychotic breaks/prophetic babbling. Ron/Hermione suspected Harry ingested it post-Felix (1996) during his “lucky” escapades. Lethal if combined with Divination exposure.

entries.name: Everlasting Elixirs
entries.content: Alchemist holy grail – constantly refills its flask if reduced below 50%. Flamel’s pre-Stone experiments failed; prototype erased its drinker’s ⏳ memories of thirst/hunger/sleep need.

entries.name: Exploding Potion
entries.content: Unstable detonating fluid brewed from 💥scarlet powder & snowdrop oil. Seamus Finnigan’s specialty (1991-1997), costing 14 cauldrons. Used in WWW’s Decoy Detonators.

entries.name: Exstimulo Potion
entries.content: Sharpens spellcasting focus / power for 15 minutes. Banned in duels since 1878 when Zabini patriarch won Championship via stack-dosing. Requires powdered leopard teeth.

entries.name: Dawdle Draught
entries.content:
Erases magical traces left by the drinker. Standard equipment for Auror fugitive hunts.


Notable Use: Sirius Black brewed it covertly as Padfoot to avoid Dark Mark trackers.

entries.name: Death Potion
entries.content:
Kills instantly through skin contact - outlawed globally in 1678.


Siege of Gringotts: Used in 1812 goblin revolt → permanently sealed vault 131's doors.

entries.name: Death-Cap Draught
entries.content: Deadly + fast-acting; turns organs to mush within hours. Brewed from Amanita virosa by post-war Death Eaters.

entries.name: Deflating Draught
entries.content: Reverses Engorgio charms and Puffapod effects. Hermione brewed for Ron after "Bloatus Maximus" disaster (1994).

entries.name: Developing Solution
entries.content:
Animates photographs (silver snake spines + crushed fireflies).


Fluid Mechanics: Must be shaken 8x counter-clockwise for fluid motion.

entries.name: Dizziness Draught
entries.content: Causes extreme imbalance within seconds. Sold by Weasleys as "Wobble Water" (1996) → banned after Peeves chaos.

entries.name: Dogbane Potion
entries.content: Poisonous to dogs/werewolves - Ministry raid prototype for Greyback capture. Penny Haywood perfected Wolfsbane alternative.

entries.name: Dogbreath Potion
entries.content: Allows fire breathing (60-second duration). WWW marketed for "drag-taming practice" but melted Seamus' tongue mug.

entries.name: Doxycide
entries.content: Paralyzes/kills doxies on contact (black tar texture).

entries.name: Dr Ubbly's Oblivious Unction
entries.content: Heals mind-inflicted injuries like Boggart burns. Neville used it post-Resurrection Stone trauma (1998). Contains powdered Diricawl feathers.

entries.name: Dragon Poison
entries.content: Weaponized venom causing liquefying necrosis. Goblins coated blades with it during 1612 rebellion. Kills in 8 hours without mermaid tears.

entries.name: Dragon Tonic
entries.content: Cures dragon pox and scale-rot. Charlie carried reserves during Norberta relocation (1991) - smells like toasted oak.

entries.name: Dragon Dung Fertilizer
entries.content: Accelerates plant growth 500%. Mandrake roots reached maturity in 4 weeks during 1993 basilisk crisis.

entries.name: Draught of Living Death
entries.content:
Potent sleeping potion mimicking death. Snape perfected it at age 16 → Dumbledore used it to fake Snape’s death (1998).


Brewing Precision: Requires moonstone slice dissolved at exact lunar zenith.

entries.name: Draught of Peace
entries.content: Calms nerves with pearlescent shimmer. Failed brew emits screaming fumes (Hermione nearly beat Snape’s record).

entries.name: Dreamless Sleep Potion
entries.content: nduces dream-deprived sleep for PTSD relief. Dumbledore secretly dosed Harry post-Cedric death (1995). Highly addictive (Lockhart overdosed).

entries.name: Drink of Despair
entries.content: See Emerald Potion entry for full lore. Voldemort’s locket guardian causing agony/memory torment.

entries.name: Drowsiness Draught
entries.content: Induces heavy eyelids within minutes. Hogwarts Hospital Wing staple for first-years with homesickness (5 max doses/yr per student).

entries.name: Fake Protective Potions
entries.content: A potion that claimed to protect the taker from Dark magic, but did not.

entries.name: Fatiguing Infusion
entries.content: A potion that, when either drank or inhaled, caused fatigue.

entries.name: Felix Felicis (Liquid Luck)
entries.content:
Nature: Metallic gold liquid inducing temporary "synchronized fortune" state.

Mechanics:


Rewires subconscious decision-making toward ideal outcomes

Overdose (>3 doses/year) causes reckless overconfidence → accidental death
Distillation: 6-month lunar infusion of Ashwinder eggs and solar-distilled thyme essence

entries.name: Fergus Fungal Budge
entries.content:
Nature: Cobalt-blue gel for Tinea draconis and magical spore infections.

Action: Crystallizes fungal networks in 8 minutes; contains powdered Billywig stingers

Note: Ineffective against non-magical fungi

entries.name: Fire-Breathing Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Scarlet-fluid triggering phosphorus-rich saliva production.

Physiology: Temporarily alters esophageal glands (60-sec duration)

Risk: 12% users develop tracheal scarring (permanent voice distortion)

entries.name: Fire Protection Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Forms invisible thermal barrier on skin/surfaces.

Composition: Salamander blood + dragon scale ash deflects 1,200°C heat

Duration: 10 minutes per dropper

entries.name: Flesh-Eating Slug Repellent
entries.content:
Nature: Odorless mist paralyzing carnivorous slugs.

Mechanism: Menthol-crystal emulsion triggers neurological shutdown

Ecological Note: Biodegrades within 48 hours

entries.name: Focus Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Ultramarine liquid enhancing neural spell recursion.

Neurochemistry: Ginkgo biloba + occamy shell → 35% faster spell recasting

Duration: 10 minutes (psychic burnout if stacked)

entries.name: Forgetfulness Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Silver-flecked vapor inducing retrograde amnesia.

Mechanism: Lethe River water targets short-term memory centers

Reversible: Only via Memoresco Charm ≤48hr post-ingestion

entries.name: Frog Parts Mixture
entries.content:
Nature: Dehydrated organics for amphibian-based potions.

Typical Composition:


Grindylow toe webbing

Ashwinder ocular lenses

Diricawl leg tendons

entries.name: Fungiface Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Accidental transfiguring contagion causing facial forests.

Pathology: Luminous Devil’s Snare spores colonize epidermis → bioluminescent growths

Cure: Submersion in Murtlap essence for 72 hours

entries.name: Garrotting Gas
entries.content:
Nature: Invisible, scentless vapor inducing immediate tracheal constriction.

Mechanics:


Paralyzes diaphragm → suffocates victims in 30 seconds

Resistant to Bubble-Head Charms; only countered by Augamenti + Ventus combo
Legacy: Banned by International Magical Convention (1717) after Bathory assassinations.

entries.name: Pepperup Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Crimson fluid curing cold/flu symptoms instantly.

Visible Effect: Steam vents from ears for 1–4 hours (indicator of potency).

Adverse Reactions: Febrile hallucinations in house-elves; not recommended for vampires.

entries.name: Germinating Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Emerald-green solution forcing hyper-accelerated plant development.

Action: One droplet sprouts mature flora in 10 seconds.

Not Herbicide: Toxic to Devil's Snare; used to purge invasive Scurvy Grass.

entries.name: Girding Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Viscous bronze liquid tripling physical resilience.

Duration: 8-hour muscle fatigue resistance; ideal for labor/Triwizard trials.

Risk: Cardiac strain in under-17 wizards (banned in school athletics).

entries.name: Grand Pepperup Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Concentrated Pepperup variant without steam side effects.

Superiority: Cures dragon pox residuals; used in St Mungo's pandemic ward (1944).

Restriction: Requires ≥8 O.W.L.s for brewing license.

entries.name: Grand Wiggenweld Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Deep-violet upgrade of Wiggenweld; stabilizes lethal injuries.

Speed: Instant coagulant (seals Sectumsempra wounds); Regrows bones in minutes.

Legend: Saved Merlin from Excalibur impalement.

entries.name: Gregory's Unctuous Unction
entries.content:
Nature: Butter-like paste commanding devotion to administrator.

Psychology: Suppresses critical thinking → irrational loyalty for 72hrs.

Dark Past: Implicated in Minister Fudge's "advisory circle" purge (1995).

entries.name: Hair-Dyeing Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Transient hair color alteration (duration: 3 days–6 weeks).

Mechanics:


Pigment Shift: Bonds with keratin → vibrates follicles to emit new hue (e.g., Weasley-red to metallic silver).

Risk: Overuse causes "Rainbow Root" syndrome (permanent multicolored streaks).

entries.name: Hair-Raising Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Induces charged hair standing vertically for 1–4 hours.

Use Case:


Defense tactic against electric eels & Lethifolds

Side Effect: Spontaneous sparks if near metal (230 recorded Gringotts vault mishaps).

entries.name: Hate Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Forces confrontation with one’s worst traits via hallucinatory self-loathing.

Psychological Effect:


Projects mental insecurities as hostile doppelgängers

Bellatrix Lestrange’s Occlumency training tool
Cure: Phoenix song + chocolate.

entries.name: Healing Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Gold-green fluid rapidly regenerating tissues/blood.

Bio-Magics:


Pulse: Restores 80% health in 15 seconds

Passive: +200% stamina recovery for 1 hour

Iconic Use: Madam Pomfrey's Hogwarts infirmary staple.

entries.name: Heartbreak Teardrops
entries.content:
**Nature": Crystal tears inducing realistic sobbing.

Properties:


Tears fluoresce neon-blue → stains skin for 24h

Distilled from Diricawl feather quills

Recalled in 1997 after Moaning Myrtle flood incident.

entries.name: Herbicide Potion
entries.content:
Composition:


Flobberworm Mucus (base)

Horclump Juice (cell dissolver)

Lionfish Spines (neurotoxin carrier)
Action: Disintegrates roots in 10 sec; banned for Venomous Tentacula poaching.

entries.name: Hiccoughing Solution
entries.content:
**Nature": Mint-flavored syrup halting hiccups instantly.

Science:


Coats phrenic nerve with Billywig-honey emulsion

Failure Rate: 3% chance of frog croaking instead of hiccups.

entries.name: Invigoration Draught
entries.content: A potion that is presumed to give the taker an energy boost.

entries.name: Invisibility Potion
entries.content: A potion that makes the taker invisible.

entries.name: Jawbind Potion
entries.content: A potion that induces lockjaw

entries.name: Kissing Concoction
entries.content:
Nature: Enchanted pink mist inducing compulsive puckering/pursed-lips syndrome (3–5 min duration).

Properties:


Delivery: Inhaled vapor or bubble-contact (identical to Beguiling Bubbles)

Effect: Forces target to blow kisses arbitrarily at nearest person/object

Side Quirk: Accidental Mimblewimble jinx if victim resists («💋 snout snout, snog about!»)
History:

Recalled twice (1996–1997) for provoking forbidden romances (e.g., Peeves ✖ Mrs. Norris)

entries.name: Laugh-Inducing Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Fluorescent orange fluid triggering extreme, involuntary laughter.

Neurology:


Targets cerebellum → overstimulates dopamine D4 receptors

Duration: 15–90 minutes (dose-dependent)
Countermeasure: Sternum-stabilizing charm prevents rib fractures from laughter spasms.

entries.name: Laxative Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Odorless blue liquid inducing rapid peristalsis.

Pharmacology:


Magically relaxes anal sphincter muscles (30–120 sec onset)

Core Agent: Powdered Dirigible Plum skins + Doxy egg extract
Medical Use: Counteracts Petrification Paralysis side-effects.

entries.name: Love Potion
entries.content: Wide spectrum (mild infatuation → debilitating obsession).

entries.name: Love Potion Antidote
entries.content:
Nature: Viscous obsidian slurry disrupting enchantment bonds.

Mechanics:


Molecular negation of Moonstone fibers in love potions

Complete Detox: Requires 3 doses over 48 hours
Limitation: Ineffective if administered 72+ hours post-exposure.

entries.name: Lung Clearing Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Menthol-cyan vapor for magical respiratory ailments.

Targeted Conditions:


Dragon-fume asphyxiation

Acromantula silk inhalation

Experimental Use: Non-magical asthma (78% success rate)
Active Compound: Distilled Occamy lung tissue.

entries.name: Oculus Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Silver-lavender elixir for magical eye trauma and curses.

Core Functions:


Sight Restoration: Repairs retinal detachment/optical nerve damage in 10 seconds.

Curse Neutralization: Dissolves Conjunctivitis Curse (suppurating pustules, photophobia).
Key Ingredient: Griffin egg albumen bonded with ground moonstone.
Critical Risk: Temporary blindness if exposed to sunlight during treatment (24-hour darkroom recovery).

entries.name: Pepperup Elixir
entries.content:
Nature: Concentrated medicinal brew with high ethanol content (46% by volume).

Key Properties:


Respiratory Relief: Clears sinus/congestion 3x faster than standard Pepperup

Dosage Limit: ≤7 drops solo or ≤21 drops diluted (Alcohol poisoning risk)

Distinction: Does not produce steam exhaust like Pepperup Potion

entries.name: Poison Antidote
entries.content:
Nature: Adaptive solution that counteracts 120+ magical toxins.

Mechanism:


Molecularly mimics poison structure → bonds/neutralizes toxins

Gaps: Ineffective against Basilisk venom or Dementor-induced spiritual decay
Base Ingredient: Powdered bezoar suspended in unicorn tears

entries.name: Polyjuice Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Thick, mutable-textured potion for temporary physical transformation.

Core Mechanics:


Duration: 1 hour per dose (12-hour max via continuous dosing → organ failure risk)

Requires fresh DNA donor sample (hair/skin: ≤48hrs old)

Interdictions: Animal DNA causes irreversible mutations; Veela blood = lethal
Brewing: 1 lunar cycle with fluxweed picked at new moon

entries.name: Pomfrey's Pick-Me-Up
entries.content:
Nature: Radiant gold fluid accelerating natural healing.

Efficacy:


Mends fractures in 2 hours

Purges minor curses (Jelly-Legs, Furnunculus)

Contains Billywig honey for pain suppression

entries.name: Pompion Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Pumpkin-orange gel inducing cephalic transmutation.

Properties:


Duration: 1-4 hours (size scales with victim's intelligence)

Speech remains possible → muffled "pumpkin mumble"

Known Use: Peeves contaminated 1994 Hallowe'en feast pumpkin juice

entries.name: Experimental Potions (No. 07 / 113 / 86 / 329 / 220)
entries.content:
No. 07: Acidic purple sludge → melts metal (wand cores vulnerable)

No. 113: Truth serum failure → compels victim to rhyme incessantly

No. 86: Contact neurotoxin → liquefies cerebellum in 10 sec (Class-X banned)

No. 329: Suspected time-altering fluid (unstable; distorts short-term memory)

No. 220: Volatile combustion agent (spontaneously ignites when agitated)

entries.name: Potion of All Potential
entries.content:
Nature: Obsidian-black liquid granting temporary mastery of innate abilities.

Effects:


Amplifies magical precision + physical prowess to theoretical limits

Crash: 48-hour exhaustion/weakness post-duration (brain fog, magic depletion)

Banned from tournaments; misuse = 10-year Azkaban sentence

entries.name: Potion of Invisibility
entries.content:
Nature: Quicksilver-textured brew coating skin in light-refracting cells.

Mechanics:


Duration: 15-90 minutes (sweat dissolves effect)

Vulnerable to: Infrared vision (dragon/Aragog), Homenum Revelio

Synergy: Doubles efficiency under Disillusionment Charm

entries.name: Venomous Tentacula Juice
entries.content:
Nature: Emerald-green sap inducing temporary neural blockade.

Mechanics:


Targets motor neurons → full-body paralysis (1-4 hour duration)

Key Use: Security measure in Gringotts vaults; diluted in Weasleys' Puking Pastilles
Antidote: Powdered Dittany + Billywig saliva (restores mobility in 2 minutes)

entries.name: Veritaserum
entries.content:
Nature: Odorless/viscosity-less liquid overriding deception.

Neurochemistry:


Onset: 17 seconds via sublingual absorption

Brain Effect: Suppresses prefrontal cortex → forces factual speech

Limit: Skilled Occlumens resist; ineffective against prophesy/memory charms
Brewing Complexity: 1 lunar cycle of clockwise stirring per drop

entries.name: Vitamix Potion
entries.content:
Nature: Carbonated copper fluid providing instant stamina.

Metabolic Action:


Muscle Recharge: ATP regeneration × 300%

Magic Boost: Faster spell-chaining for 15 minutes

Unique Trait: Flavor adapts to drinker's preference (based on mood)
Legacy: Basis for Pepperup Elixir (1948 patent dispute)

entries.name: Volubilis Potion
entries.content: Violet shimmering syrup altering laryngeal resonance.

entries.name: Wizarding Schools
entries.content:
Origins & Purpose

Pre-Historic Roots: Early magical education occurred through familial apprenticeships or solitary study. Formal schools emerged as secrecy became imperative during global witch hunts (e.g., Salem Witch Trials, Medieval European persecutions).

Core Mission: To safeguard young witches/wizards, teach controlled magic, prevent accidental exposure to Muggles, and preserve endangered magical practices.

Global Governance & Classification

Oversight: Regulated by the International Confederation of Wizards (ICW). All schools must adhere to the International Statute of Wizarding Secrecy.

The "Great Eleven":
ICW officially recognizes 11 elite institutions (e.g., Hogwarts, Uagadou, Ilvermorny).
Unregistered schools operate covertly but lack accreditation and resources.

Ministry Influence: National Ministries (e.g., British Ministry of Magic) enforce local attendance laws, curriculum standards, and homeschool inspections.

Common Characteristics

Admission & Age:

Automatic identification via magical trace (activated by underage magic).
Enrollment begins at age 11, lasting 7 years (exceptions: Mahoutokoro starts at 7).
Acceptance notifications use arcane methods (e.g., dreams at Uagadou, enchanted letters at Hogwarts).

Curriculum & Specialization:

Core Subjects: Transfiguration, Charms, Potions, Defense Against the Dark Arts.
Regional Focus:
Wandless Magic (Uagadou, Africa).
Magizoology Integration (Castelobruxo, South America).
Cultural Wizardry Studies (Koldovstoretz, Eurasia).
Evaluation: Standardized exams (e.g., O.W.L.s/N.E.W.T.s) determine career paths.

Secrecy & Security:

Concealment Enchantments:
Unplottability, Muggle-Repelling Charms, terrain illusions (e.g., fog-shrouded castles, disappearing islands).
Remote Locations: Built in magically fortified zones (mountains, jungles, tundras).

Culture & Tradition:

House Systems: Foster loyalty via competitive cohorts (e.g., Hogwarts' Gryffindor, Ilvermorny's Thunderbird).
Sport: Quidditch is universally played; variants adapt to local environments (e.g., dense-forest broom courses).
Ethics: Dark Arts taught as theoretical defense, not practice (strictly forbidden at Durmstrang post-Grindelwald).

Governance Structure

Headmaster/Headmistress: Highest authority over staff and students.

Board of Governors: Includes Ministry officials, alumni, and distinguished wizards who approve budgets and policies.

Hogwarts-Specific Note: The British Minister for Magic cannot directly intervene in school affairs (per Hogwarts Charter of 1329).

Non-Traditional Education

Homeschooling: Permitted with Ministry monitoring (e.g., the Weasley children pre-Hogwarts).

Correspondence Courses: For geographically isolated students (mandatory until age 17 in some regions).

Apprenticeships: Post-graduation specialization (e.g., Healers at St. Mungo’s, Auror training).

entries.name: Beauxbatons Academy of Magic
entries.content:
Founding & Ethos

Established: c. 1290s by French alchemists.

Founders: Papillonlisse Fontaine (Veela-descended enchantress) & Clovis Mercœur (master wandmaker).

Motto: "Magicae Artes, Grazia Eterna" ("Magical Arts, Eternal Grace").

Philosophy: Magic as high art — precision, aestheticism, and intellectual elegance above brute force.

Campus & Architecture
Feature	Description
Location	Pyrenees Mountains, France-Spain border; concealed by glacier-mist illusions.
Structure	Palais d'Étoiles ("Palace of Stars") — White marble château with enchanted iridescent rooftops that shift hue with seasons.
Gardens	Orangerie Enchantée: Sentient frost-resistant orchards providing potion ingredients.
Iconic Element	Fontaine Sacrée: Sapphire fountain (healing waters) where the Flame of Acceptance ignites admissions.
Academics
Curriculum Distinctions

Core Excellence:

Alchemy: Taught since 1321; Nicolas Flamel was Chair (1402-1418). Advanced students brew Philosopher’s Stone simulacra.
Charm-Weaving: Combines spellcraft with haute couture (e.g., self-stitching robes, emotion-reactive fabrics).
Culinary Enchantment: Pastry conjuration as precision magic (elective).
